params.series: {metro name: index file} plus a national file
params.buyYear: year whose 4 quarterly values are averaged as the purchase base
params.saleQuarter: quarter-start date of the sale value (must be the last observation of every index file)
params.cpiNowMonth: YYYY-MM-01 (latest month in the CPI file)

newKindNeeds.computation: For each index series s, growth g_s = index(saleQuarter) / mean(index of the four quarters of buyYear) (exactly four values required). The break-even 2000 purchase price is T_s = exclusion / (g_s - 1): a home bought at P that rose like the index has gain P(g_s - 1) at saleQuarter, which exceeds the exclusion exactly when P > T_s (no improvements, selling costs or depreciation). Joint thresholds are computed for every metro and the national index, the single threshold for the national index only. Counts are the number of metros (national index excluded) with unrounded T_s below each cutoff; min and max are over metros. The limit in today's prices is exclusionJoint x CPI(cpiNowMonth) / CPI(cpiBaseMonth). Rounding only at output: g to 4 decimals, T to $100, the CPI restatement to $1,000.
invariants: T_s x (g_s - 1) = exclusionJoint for every series (unrounded, |error| < 1e-6)
g_s > 1 for every series (else no threshold exists)
threshold_joint_min_usd and threshold_joint_max_usd equal one of the metro thresholds; min <= every metro threshold <= max
saleQuarter is the last observation of every index file and equals sources.json lastObservation.date; cpiNowMonth is the last CPI observation
buyYear has exactly 4 quarterly observations in every index file
